transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ian Morales (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Kim (Aurum Head of ML), Rajiv Sharma (CTO), Maya Lopez (Procurement), Tom Baxter (Infra)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Discussed renewal timing, potential 20-35% capacity uplift, addition of EU region and private VPC for EU data residency, timeline for SOC2 + KMS integration, pricing sensitivity around committed vs burst. Agreed to pilot benchmark and share security pack.

Topics (auto): renewal timing; region add (EU); private deployment and KMS; cost vs latency tradeoffs; procurement timeline.

00:00 Ian Morales: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, starting a little after 3. Um quick out of the gate, Leah can you confirm priorities for this quarter from your side?
00:12 Leah Kim: Yeah hi thanks Ian, priorities are continuity for our chat assistants, lower token cost for high-volume pipelines, and we have an upcoming compliance push — EU data residency for Q3, so multi-region is a must.
00:26 Rajiv Sharma: Also want predictable latency for EU customers; we've seen some tail spikes with our current provider during peak.
00:33 Sana Patel: Got it, main things we'll focus on today are the commitment uplift you mentioned in email, options for adding an EU cluster (hosted vs private VPC), and a quick look at what latency/cost trade we expect.
00:47 Maya Lopez: Procurement timeline — we need to decide on a renewal by end of March to align budgets. So cost detail is critical.
00:55 Ian Morales: Understood. Before we jump in — quick intros, Sana's our solutions engineer who ran the initial benchmarks last quarter and will own the tech plan.
01:04 Sana Patel: hey all, thanks. I'll flag where we typically see wins from batching, KV cache, and quant variants.
01:14 Tom Baxter: can you summarize which models you tested last time? I think the spreadsheet said redwood-2-medium and an optimized open model?
01:23 Sana Patel: yeah we ran redwood-2-small and a 8-bit quant of OpenLM-3 for the high-throughput endpoints. The small model hit our cost targets with some latency amplification on long contexts.
01:36 Leah Kim: Our main production is a reranking + assistant flow, usually 512 tokens average.
01:42 Ian Morales: Perfect. So on renewal size — you flagged a 20% lift in the form we talked about, but Rajiv mentioned more, what's comfortable?
01:53 Rajiv Sharma: We're forecasting 30-35% depending on retention push. We'd like reserved capacity for predictability but need to keep room for bursts.
02:03 Ian Morales: We can propose a committed tier plus burst pool. Typical structure: baseline reserved for steady QPS, burst credits for seasonal or marketing pushes. Pricing-wise we can tier discounts at 25%/35% commit.
02:18 Maya Lopez: Would you be able to show numbers? Procurement can't sign without concrete delta to existing invoice.
02:25 Ian Morales: I'll send a two-tier quote: conservative (25% reserved) and aggressive (35% reserved). I'll include per-token list and burst pricing.
02:33 Maya Lopez: thanks. EOS is end of March so need the doc Monday.
02:38 Ian Morales: Yep aim for 2027-03-18 delivery.
02:42 [00:03:00] Sana Patel: On region work — EU requirement, you have two paths: Hosted EU region on Redwood, or Private VPC in your cloud account. Hosted is fastest (we can turn on region within 2–3 weeks once contract binds). Private VPC takes longer — provisioning, networking review with your infra, and KMS/HSM integration.
03:00 Tom Baxter: For private, how do you handle traffic egress and NAT? Are you expecting us to manage transit?
03:07 Sana Patel: Typically customers bring their own NAT/Transit and we peer to the VPC. We'll provide a deployment manifest, and our private control plane handles scheduling. There's a short checklist for subnets, EIPs, and KMS endpoints.
03:20 Rajiv Sharma: KMS is big for us. We need to keep keys in our HSM and ensure no plaintext tokens leave. Do you support customer-managed CMKs?
03:29 Sana Patel: Yes — customer-managed CMKs are supported; we have an HSM integration pattern. We'll share the KMS integration doc. Note: there are a few edge cases on log forwarding when using private control plane, we'll call those out.
03:42 Leah Kim: Also, audit logs for prompt/response retention — we don't want raw prompts persisted in any long-term store in EU. Is that configurable?
03:51 Sana Patel: You can configure retention and choose to mask or drop prompt bodies before logs leave the VPC. We'll include our audit log policy and the steps to enforce minimal retention.
04:02 Maya Lopez: From procurement perspective, what's the SLA for private vs hosted?
04:08 Ian Morales: Hosted typically has standard SLA at 99.9; private can be contracted up to 99.95 with the Dedicated package and a higher commitment. We'll include SLA options in the quote.
04:20 [00:10:00] Leah Kim: On latency — can you give ballpark numbers for EU-hosted vs private in-region?
04:27 Sana Patel: In-region private or hosted EU cluster, 95th percentile is usually 70–120 ms per token for our optimized small/medium families on A100-like hardware; hosted multi-tenant may have slightly higher tail under heavy load. The biggest wins for latency are continuous batching and local KV cache.
04:45 Rajiv Sharma: That 70–120ms — is that for generation or for embeddings? Our core UX is text generation.
04:51 Sana Patel: Generation — with 512 token contexts, single-stream latency at 95th. Embeddings are lower, sub-50ms typically.
04:59 Ian Morales: On cost, quantization can knock down per-token cost 20–40% depending on model. But we surface potential quality regressions — we'd recommend a small eval run.
05:11 Leah Kim: We do rely on output quality, can't have hallucinations spike. We'll need guardrails and eval sets.
05:18 Sana Patel: Agreed. We can run your evals during the pilot and add regression alerts via Redwood Optimize.
05:25 [00:15:00] Maya Lopez: Competitors — just to be transparent — we're also talking to NimbusAI about a private EU deployment. Their pitch is cheaper burst but they don't have the same KV cache stuff.
05:36 Ian Morales: Noted. We typically compete on predictable unit economics and operational features.
05:41 Tom Baxter: A couple of technical clarifications — how do you handle model rollbacks and canarying in private? We need A/Bing without flipping global traffic.
05:50 Sana Patel: We support canary rollouts within private deployments; traffic can be routed per-route, per-model. You can pin versions for specific endpoints and sweep once metrics look good.
06:01 Rajiv Sharma: For the pilot benchmark — do you need us to provide synthetic traffic or can Redwood generate?
06:06 Sana Patel: Ideally both. Provide a replay of production trace for realistic load, and we'll seed synthetic spikes to test autoscaling and burst behavior. Tom, the team will need an S3 or stream of traces and a sample of prompt shapes.
06:18 Tom Baxter: We'll get that to you — I can aim to share an anonymized trace by 2027-03-19.
06:23 Leah Kim: On timeline — if we sign by end of March, what does a conservative rollout look like for EU?
06:29 Ian Morales: Sign end of March -> activate EU hosted pool early April (2–3 weeks) -> pilot benchmark mid-late April -> private VPC pilot in May if you choose that path. It's a two-track plan to avoid blocking.
06:40 Maya Lopez: Procurement questions: termination, data egress fees, and audit support — can you put those clauses in a sample SOW?
06:48 Ian Morales: We'll attach SOW samples and typical termination language; egress depends on private hosting and cloud provider. We'll surface an estimate.
06:55 [00:20:00] Sana Patel: A couple of gotchas — if you lean on quantized models for cost, we should lock a regression threshold in your evals. And prefix caching helps a lot, but requires stable prompt patterns.
07:08 Leah Kim: Our assistant flow has lots of short-turn prefixed system prompts — caching should work well.
07:14 Rajiv Sharma: What about token accounting differences — we saw variance across providers on how they count special tokens.
07:19 Ian Morales: We explain tokenization in the pricing sheet; we'll include a worked example for your 512 token median request.
07:25 Maya Lopez: On billing cadence — monthly invoice with usage reconciliation?
07:29 Ian Morales: Yes monthly with an upfront reserved commit charge for the reserved capacity portion.
07:33 Tom Baxter: For private VPC, do you require particular instance types? We run on custom machine types.
07:39 Sana Patel: We provide a matrix of compatible hardware families; we can run on standard NVIDIA A100 or equivalent. For on-prem/edge there are specifics we'll list.
07:48 Leah Kim: Security — we'll need SOC2, ISO attestation and penetration test results. Also SOC2 for hosted EU cluster?
07:55 Ian Morales: We'll share SOC2 Type II report and pen-test summary. Hosted or private, we maintain the same compliance posture for the control plane; private may add extra artifacts for your infra.
08:05 Maya Lopez: Anything else on procurement?
08:08 Maya Lopez: Also need references from similar financial customers.
08:11 Ian Morales: I can share two references — a mid-market fintech and a payments company who did the EU private rollout last year.
08:17 [00:30:00] Leah Kim: Quick question about fallbacks — if EU cluster enters degraded state, can traffic route to US with redaction? We need graceful degradation.
08:26 Sana Patel: Yes — you can configure fallback policies. We also support on-the-fly redaction at the edge if you need to remove PII before crossing boundaries.
08:35 Rajiv Sharma: Good. One concern — network egress latency when failing over to US might break some UX. Can you set lower-priority routes?
08:42 Sana Patel: You can set routing policies by latency, cost, or hard-affinity. For UX-sensitive endpoints, we'll keep hard-affinity to EU and only fall back for non-critical batch jobs.
08:52 Tom Baxter: For the benchmark session, what's the expected Redwood involvement? Full-day run?
08:56 Sana Patel: Typically 2 hours hands-on to validate config and then we run 24–48 hour soak with periodic check-ins. We'll need your infra contact on the call.
09:06 Ian Morales: Recap and next steps: we'll send two-tiered pricing and SOW samples, Sana will share private control plane checklist and KMS notes, and Aurum will provide traces for benchmarking. Proposed dates — pricing docs by 2027-03-18, traces by 2027-03-19, benchmark week of 2027-03-22.
09:23 Maya Lopez: That timeline works; procurement can review initial terms once we have the SOW.
09:28 Leah Kim: Can we get a follow-up tech deep dive with your SEs after the benchmark results?
09:32 Sana Patel: Absolutely, we'll schedule a post-benchmark deep dive to review regressions and rollout plan.
09:38 Ian Morales: Anything else from the Aurum side?
09:40 Rajiv Sharma: No, thanks. We'll review the docs and sync.
09:44 Ian Morales: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Auto action summary (machine): Items captured — pricing, SOW, KMS doc, traces, benchmark schedule.

End of meeting.
